card.intuition: Everything the model sees on each request — a single finite sequence of tokens: the system prompt, the conversation so far, and every tool result fed back in. It's the only surface through which the model perceives anything; if a fact isn't in the sequence, the model doesn't know it exists.
card.analogy: A whiteboard with a fixed number of dry-erase lines: each turn scribbles more onto it until it's full, and any new fact must erase or squeeze out something already written.
card.time_complexity: The model re-reads the entire context on every turn, so cost and latency grow with context size per request.
card.space_complexity: The context window is a finite token budget; everything loaded competes for it, and overflow means truncation, compaction, or handoff.
when_to_use: Choosing which files the task touches instead of pasting the whole repo into the prompt
Budgeting input: treat the window as a token budget and load only what the task needs
Bringing anything else in via a tool call rather than direct pasting
gotchas: It is finite — a long session eventually hits the limit, forcing compaction or clearing
It is not memory: the window is working state and does not persist across sessions, unlike a memory system layered on top

steps.label: Open window
steps.annotation: A request begins with its finite token budget for this turn.

steps.label: System prompt
steps.annotation: The system prompt is prepended and consumes tokens on every request.

steps.label: History + tools
steps.annotation: Messages and tool results accumulate, each competing for the remaining budget.

steps.label: Budget hits
steps.annotation: The window fills and something must go: truncation, compaction, or handoff.

steps.label: Reset / handoff
steps.annotation: Clearing or compacting starts a new bounded window for the next session.

exercise.prompt: Estimate whether a snippet fits in the remaining context-window token budget (rough rule: 4 characters per token).
hints: Compare your rough token estimate against the remaining budget.
The snippet fits if it consumes no more tokens than remain.
